Quick initial read from the traces Maria sent: we've got clear signs of sustained batching windows expanding for many small requests. Timeline matches a rollout at 17:30 that changed the default batching policy for that model family — the kernel now prefers larger batch sizes to improve throughput, but we missed a short-tail workload signal. The runtime is aggregating requests until a larger batch size or timeout is reached, causing queue depth to grow and raising tail latency.

Proposed immediate mitigations (what I can do now):
1) Reduce the batch hold time from 12ms -> 3ms for Acme's model instance (hotfix toggle).
2) Temporarily pin traffic to the previous batching profile (safer).
3) If traffic is very bursty, route ~20% of Acme traffic to a lower-batch, lower-latency pool (capacity permitting).

I'll prepare a config flip and warm up a fallback pool. Can execute in ~10–15 mins once we confirm bridge details.

— Dylan Brooks
Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-bridge summary and action items — Acme Health latency incident

Team — summary from today's bridge and agreed actions: 

What happened:
- 17:30 PDT rollout changed the default batching profile for the model family serving Acme, causing the runtime to favor larger batch aggregation. Short-tail traffic encountered extended wait times, increasing queue_depth and tail latencies (p95/p99).

Immediate mitigations performed during bridge:
- Dylan rolled back the batching profile for Acme's production route to previous settings (hold time 3ms) at 18:57 PDT.
- We routed 25% of traffic to a low-batch pool for 40 minutes as a safety valve.
- Marissa engaged SRE to watch capacity and alerted billing/partner teams.

Observed outcome:
- p95 dropped from 1.8s to ~220ms within 3 minutes of the rollback; p99 dropped below 600ms after the safety routing. Queue depth returned to baseline (~35) after 12 minutes.

Follow-ups and owner list:
- Dylan: add a short-tail workload detector that prevents aggressive batching profile flips for routes with median latency < 300ms (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Evelyn (Product): evaluate rollout gating to include queue_depth and tail-latency checks (ETA: 1 week).
- Marissa: coordinate a customer-facing RCA and share a timeline for permanent fixes (ETA: 48 hours).
- Jonas: keep Acme point-of-contact looped and provide daily status until RCA is shared.

Attachments: bridge transcript, live graphs (linked in incident doc).

Maria — apologies again for the disruption. We'll follow up with the RCA and changes to rollout policy. Please reach out if you see any regression.

— Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
